subject: maths
title: Chapter 6 · Test 1
summary: Chapter 6 test 1: index laws, zero and negative indices, scientific notation, introducing surds and simplifying surds.
body:
This test covers all of Chapter 6, Indices and surds: the index laws, zero and negative indices, scientific notation, what surds are and how to estimate them, and simplifying, adding and multiplying surds.

There are 15 questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes, no notes, no calculator unless the question says. Write your working on paper. Give exact answers as surds in simplest form, and check that scientific notation answers have one non-zero digit before the decimal point. When you finish, check any you got wrong using the steps and the notes on each wrong answer.

questions.explanation: Same base, multiplying: add the indices, 7 + 2 = 9, so b⁹. b¹⁴ multiplies the indices instead.
steps: Same base b, multiplying, so add the indices.

mistakes.A: Step 1: multiplying powers with the same base means add the indices, not multiply them.
mistakes.C: Step 1: subtract only when dividing. Here the powers are multiplied.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the two powers join into one; there is no coefficient of 2.

questions.explanation: 3⁻² = 1/3² = 1/9. −9 treats the negative index as a minus sign.
steps: A negative index means one over: 3⁻² = 1/3².

mistakes.A: Step 1: a negative index means the reciprocal, not a negative number.
mistakes.B: Step 1: don't multiply the base by the index. 3⁻² means 1 ÷ 3².

questions.explanation: From 7.2 to 72 000 000 the point moves 7 places right, so 7.2 × 10⁷. 7.2 × 10⁶ counts the 6 zeros instead of the 7 moves.
steps: Put the point after the first digit: 7.2.
The point moves 7 places right to get back to 72 000 000, so 7.2 × 10⁷.

mistakes.B: Step 2: count the places the point moves (7), not the zeros (6).
mistakes.C: Step 1: the first number must be at least 1 and less than 10.
mistakes.D: Step 2: a large number needs a positive index.

questions.prompt: Between which two whole numbers does √50 lie?
questions.explanation: 49 is less than 50 and 50 is less than 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8. 25 and 26 halves 50 instead of square rooting it.
steps: Find the perfect squares either side of 50: 7² = 49 and 8² = 64.
49 is less than 50, which is less than 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8.

mistakes.A: Step 1: a square root is not half the number. Look for perfect squares near 50.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 7² = 49 is less than 50, so √50 is more than 7.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 8² = 64 is more than 50, so √50 is less than 8.

steps: The outside index goes to every factor: (3m⁴)² = 3² × (m⁴)².

mistakes.B: Step 1: the index 2 applies to the 3 as well — 3² = 9.
mistakes.D: Step 3: (m⁴)² is a power of a power, so multiply the indices (4 × 2), not add them.

questions.prompt: Simplify y² ÷ y⁶ and write your answer with a positive index.
questions.explanation: y² ÷ y⁶ = y²⁻⁶ = y⁻⁴ = 1/y⁴. y⁴ comes from subtracting the wrong way round.
steps: Same base, dividing, so subtract in order: 2 − 6 = −4, giving y⁻⁴.

mistakes.A: Step 1: subtract in the order written: 2 − 6, not 6 − 2.
mistakes.B: Step 2: a negative index means the reciprocal, not a minus sign in front.
mistakes.D: Step 1: dividing powers means subtract the indices, not divide them.

questions.explanation: a = 3.05 and the point moves 3 places left, so 3.05 × 10⁻³. 3.05 × 10⁻² counts zeros instead of moves.
steps: The first non-zero digit is 3, so a = 3.05.
From 3.05 to 0.003 05 the point moves 3 places left, so 3.05 × 10⁻³.

mistakes.A: Step 2: count the places the point moves (3), not the zeros after the point (2).
mistakes.C: Step 1: the 0 between 3 and 5 is significant — keep it.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the first number must be at least 1 and less than 10.

questions.explanation: √20 = √4 × √5 = 2√5. 4√5 takes the 4 out without square rooting it.
steps: The largest perfect square factor of 20 is 4 (20 = 4 × 5).

mistakes.A: Step 2: only the square root of 4 comes out: √4 = 2.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 20 = 4 × 5, so 4 is the perfect square. You swapped the factors.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 20 = 10 × 2 doesn't help — 10 is not a perfect square.

mistakes.A: Step 1: multiply the numbers under the root (2 × 18), don't add them.
mistakes.B: Step 2: √36 = 6 — don't forget to take the square root.
mistakes.D: Step 1: this is a multiplication — you divided 18 by 2.

questions.prompt: Find the exact length of x in this right-angled triangle.
questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with shorter sides 5 cm (base) and 2 cm (height); the hypotenuse is labelled x.
questions.explanation: x² = 5² + 2² = 25 + 4 = 29, so x = √29 cm (29 has no perfect-square factor). 29 cm forgets the square root.
steps: x = √29 cm, and 29 has no perfect-square factor, so this is exact and simplest.

mistakes.B: Step 1: Pythagoras squares the sides first: 5² + 2², not 5 + 2.
mistakes.C: Step 1: square each side before adding: 5² + 2² = 29, not 5 + 2 = 7.
mistakes.D: Step 2: x² = 29, so take the square root to find x.

questions.prompt: Calculate (2.5 × 10⁴) × (6 × 10⁻⁷). Give your answer in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: 2.5 × 6 = 15 and 10⁴ × 10⁻⁷ = 10⁻³, so 15 × 10⁻³ = 1.5 × 10⁻². 1.5 × 10⁻³ forgets to adjust the index.

mistakes.A: Step 3: when 15 becomes 1.5, the index goes up by 1: −3 + 1 = −2.
mistakes.B: Step 2: multiplying powers of 10 means add the indices (4 + −7), not multiply them.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 15 is not between 1 and 10 — adjust it to 1.5.

questions.explanation: √27 = 3√3, so 2√3 + 3√3 = 5√3. 11√3 takes 9 out of the root instead of 3.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you can't add under the root. Simplify √27 first.
mistakes.C: Step 2: write √27 in simplest form and add like surds — don't add 12 + 27 under one root.
mistakes.D: Step 1: √27 = √9 × √3 = 3√3. Only the root of 9 comes out, not 9.

questions.prompt: This square has an area of 32 cm². Find the exact side length s, in simplest surd form.
questions.diagram_alt: A square labelled Area = 32 cm², with its side labelled s.
questions.explanation: s = √32 = √16 × √2 = 4√2 cm. 8 cm divides the area by 4, which mixes up area and perimeter.
steps: Area = s², so s² = 32 and s = √32.

mistakes.A: Step 2: √32 = √16 × √2, and √16 = 4 — take the root of 16.
mistakes.B: Step 1: the side is the square root of the area, not the area divided by 4.
mistakes.D: Step 1: don't divide the area by 4 — the side of a square is √(area).

questions.prompt: Find the value of n if 5ⁿ = 1/125.
questions.explanation: 125 = 5³, so 1/125 = 5⁻³ and n = −3. n = 3 forgets the reciprocal.
steps: Write 125 as a power of 5: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so 125 = 5³.

mistakes.B: Step 2: 5³ = 125, but 1/125 is its reciprocal, which needs a negative index.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 125 ÷ 5 = 25 isn't the index. Count how many 5's multiply to make 125.
mistakes.D: Step 2: a reciprocal comes from a negative index, not a fraction index.

questions.explanation: (x⁵)² = x¹⁰, then x¹⁰ ÷ x³ = x⁷. x⁴ adds the indices in the bracket instead of multiplying.

mistakes.A: Step 1: (x⁵)² is a power of a power — multiply 5 × 2, don't add 5 + 2.
mistakes.B: Step 2: dividing by x³ means subtract 3, not add it.
mistakes.D: Step 1: multiply the indices (5 × 2 = 10); don't square the index (5² = 25).
